newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nisseki House says not hurt by management move.
newsitem.headline: Nisseki House says not hurt by management move.

text.p: Nisseki House Industry Co Ltd said on Tuesday that steps taken to cope with the effects of the disappearance of its president had not had any negative impact on its business.
"We would like to stress that this has not in any way had a negative impact on our overall business," vice president Yuji Horiuchi said in a statement.

Last week Nisseki House, which makes prefabricated houses, created a new post of vice president because it had not been able to contact its president, Saburo Horiuchi, since December 11. Managing director Yuji Horiuchi was appointed vice president.
Nisseki House shares continued to slump on the Tokyo stock market on Tuesday, ending 46 yen lower at 204 yen. Traders said sales were prompted by uncertainty over its management.

"We strongly believe that our strong efforts during the past year to rationalise and strengthen our business will secure a stable and profitable business environment for the future of Nisseki House," the statement said.
The company is in close contact with its banks, including Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd, the statement added without elaborating.
Earlier on Tuesday, a Nisseki official told Reuters that the company did not know Horiuchi's whereabouts, but that this would not affect its management or financing situation.
Nisseki House also said in a statement that its converible notes were trading at unsatisfactory levels.

"...possibly as a result of the overall weakness of Japanese stock markets as well as Japan Credit Rating Agency's downgrading of our domestic nine billion yen convertible bonds due March 2001 from BBB to BB, we have noticed that our two outstanding Swiss franc convertible note issues are trading at levels we feel do not adequately represent our financial standing," it said.
